log.why: Test the leading candidate dnaK (0.395) directly; a positive result will give high confidence to publish.
Testing 10 µM bisects the threshold prior near its median while Ticket 1's plate incubates.
Testing 3 uM splits the posterior mass (~0.57 vs 0.43) evenly, maximizing information while we publish Ticket 1 during incubation.
Testing {gyrA, recA} splits Ticket 3's prior nearly in half (0.471) and incubates while we publish Ticket 1.
Treat at 1 uM to split the 0.441 probability at or below 1 uM from the 0.483 lead at 3 uM while using free incubators.
Testing gyrA directly separates the tied top candidates gyrA and recA while letting the plate incubate before publishing Ticket 1.
Testing {lacZ, sodA} splits Ticket 4's prior nearly in half (0.476) and lets the plate incubate while we publish Ticket 1.
E0 strongly supports dnaK at 0.880 posterior with little time left, securing high bonuses and freeing a ticket slot.
Test recA directly on urgent Ticket 3 now so it can incubate while we publish Ticket 2.
Ticket 2 has only 10s left and strong 0.793 posterior for 3 µM after responses at 3/10 µM and none at 1 µM.
With 9s left no new plate can finish, and publishing gyrA at 0.261 beats the -30 expiration penalty in expectation.
Ticket 4 expires soon and is split between sodA and lacZ; testing lacZ cleanly resolves the top two candidates before publishing.
E3 bisects Ticket 6's prior (0.408 <= 3 uM) into four low and four high doses while Ticket 4's E0 finishes incubating.
Ticket 4 has strong posterior support for lacZ (0.889) and only 4 seconds remaining before expiration.
Testing 10 µM on Ticket 6 splits its top hypotheses (10 µM vs higher doses) with enough round time left to publish.
Testing metJ maximizes single-plate expected accuracy on Ticket 7 while Ticket 6 finishes E4, leaving time to publish both before round end.
With only 2 seconds left in the round, we immediately publish Ticket 6 since 10 µM has a strong 0.699 posterior from E3 and E4.
